Successful payment confirms the order and generates tickets
Failed payment releases the hold and does not generate tickets

The exact same webhook event delivered twice is processed exactly once

scenario: End-to-end: register -> browse -> reserve -> checkout -> fake pay -> ticket page with QR
A customer cannot release another customer's hold
The same reservation checked out twice sequentially returns the existing order, never a second one
The same reservation checked out concurrently (several requests) still produces exactly one order
provider.createPayment failing leaves the reservation checked out against one order/payment, and a retry recovers without duplicating it
A payment_events row claimed but never marked processed (simulated interruption) is reprocessed, not silently acknowledged as a duplicate
A failed event after an already-succeeded event never overwrites Payment.status or revokes tickets
A succeeded event after an already-failed event never retroactively generates tickets
Simultaneous succeeded and failed events for the same payment settle on exactly one outcome, never both
A validly-signed webhook claiming the wrong amount is rejected (409, audit-logged), no ticket generated
A validly-signed webhook claiming the wrong currency is rejected, no ticket generated
Cancelling a hold after its checkout has started (order/payment exist) is refused (409), stock stays reserved

The fake webhook, simulate route, and pay page all refuse to operate when NODE_ENV=production without the explicit opt-in; getPaymentProvider throws (which instrumentation.ts uses to fail server boot)
note: Also manually verified end-to-end: `next start` with NODE_ENV=production and PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake crashes at boot without the opt-in, and boots normally with ALLOW_FAKE_PAYMENTS_IN_PRODUCTION=true (used by the Playwright e2e webServer).

Creating a hold is refused for an inactive TicketCategory
Creating a hold is refused for an inactive SalesPhase, or outside its start/end window
A SalesPhase's phaseQuantityLimit is enforced atomically even when several buyers race for it concurrently
A per-user/event purchase limit cannot be bypassed by splitting one purchase into several separate holds, including across different ticket categories of the same event and under concurrency
A payment.succeeded after an already-failed order is fulfilled directly (paid, ticket generated) when inventory is still available
A payment.succeeded after an already-failed order becomes reconciliation_required (no ticket, no oversell) once the stock was resold, while Payment.status still reflects the captured money
A payment.succeeded after an already-cancelled order is reconciled the same way as failed-then-succeeded
Both reconciliation outcomes (fulfilled, or requires-reconciliation) create a distinct AuditLog entry
Concurrent checkout requests for the same reservation call provider.createPayment exactly once, not merely produce one database Order
provider.createPayment fails, the hold expires and is swept, then a retry does not call the provider again and returns an explicit HOLD_EXPIRED error
The same expired-retry refusal holds even when the background sweep hasn't run yet (lazy expires_at check)
An expired-but-unswept hold does not keep consuming the user's purchase allowance, and inventory is released exactly once when the next hold's lock touches that category
The same exclusion works for an expired-but-unswept hold in a different category of the same event, without requiring that category's own lock to run
An event id previously seen with an invalid signature is never reprocessed as valid by a later, correctly-signed attempt under the same id
Reclaiming an interrupted event whose resolved payment differs from the originally-claimed payment is rejected as an inconsistent collision, audited, neither order affected
Reclaiming an interrupted event whose event type differs from what was originally claimed is rejected as an inconsistent collision
No accidental EL-Bied-Ali/Hello-html links exist anywhere in this repository

A genuine ticket presented for another event returns WRONG_EVENT without exposing attendee details
Unauthenticated customers and support-only staff cannot call the ticket validation endpoint
Scanner staff can sign in, select an event, and submit a QR token from the mobile scanner interface
Only admin/super-admin can mutate the catalogue while support remains read-only
Category capacity cannot be reduced below sold plus currently reserved inventory
Two active sales phases in one category cannot have overlapping windows
A sales phase cap cannot be lowered below already sold or live-reserved quantities
Direct event cancellation is blocked while issued tickets, live holds or pending payments exist
A successful catalogue mutation and its audit record commit in the same transaction
A purchase waiting on an admin catalogue edit revalidates the new state before reserving stock
A draft event created in the admin catalogue returns 404 on its public URL
CSV export cells starting with =, +, -, or @ are neutralized so spreadsheet apps never execute them as formulas
CSV export cells containing commas, quotes, or newlines are correctly quoted and escaped
Audit log entries authored by an admin resolve to that admin's display name; system entries with no actor never crash resolution
Filtering the audit log by entity type returns only matching entries
Cursor-based audit log pagination visits every row exactly once, across pages
The orders CSV export includes the fields needed for reconciliation and respects a status filter
Admin and support accounts can view the audit log and export orders as CSV; a scanner account is forbidden from both
A full refund transitions payment/order to refunded, cancels every still-valid ticket, and releases its stock for resale
A partial refund transitions payment/order to partially_refunded without cancelling tickets or touching inventory
A second partial refund that completes the remaining balance transitions to fully refunded and only then cancels tickets
A refund amount greater than the remaining refundable balance is rejected without changing payment status
Refunding a payment that was never paid, or one already fully refunded, is rejected (duplicate-refund guard)

A full refund never cancels an already-used ticket or double-releases its stock, only the still-valid ones

Calling the order-confirmation email trigger twice for the same order sends exactly one email
Calling the payment-failed email trigger twice for the same order sends exactly one email
An email provider send failure is recorded (no providerMessageId) without throwing out of the trigger or blocking unrelated sends
The payment webhook sends an order-confirmation email exactly once, even when a second (differently-IDed) succeeded event arrives for the same already-settled order
The payment webhook sends a payment-failed email when the payment fails

Every email trigger is a silent no-op for an unknown order/refund id rather than throwing
checkRateLimit allows exactly the configured number of calls within a window and rejects the next
checkRateLimit resets once a new fixed window starts
Different rate-limit keys never share a bucket
checkRateLimit never lets more than the configured limit through under concurrent calls on the same key
Repeated registration attempts for one normalized email are limited even when the source IP changes, while another email remains independent
Admin login is limited per account across changing IPs before credential verification; rejection includes Retry-After/reset metadata
Customer login is limited per account across changing IPs; exceeding it throws RATE_LIMITED instead of evaluating credentials
Rate-limit keys are deterministic but never contain the raw IP address or account email
Platform-owned Vercel IP is preferred; malformed values collapse to unknown and equivalent IPv6 forms canonicalize to one identity
Rejected buckets cap at limit + 1 and return Retry-After plus reset/remaining metadata
Production refuses a missing/weak HMAC secret and refuses disabled rate limiting without the explicit isolated-test opt-in
